News & Analysis on Domestic and International Trade, National and State Finances, Budget, Government Regulation, Monetary Policy, RBI Rates, Interest Rates, CRR, Indian Trade, Monetary and Industrial Policy.

item.title: Eye on the price: Retail inflation at 5.54% in September, most on new base
item.description: India's retail inflation increased to 5.54% year-on-year in September, the highest since January. This rise is attributed to higher food prices, particularly onions and other essentials. Economists predict inflation could approach 6% in the coming months, influencing upcoming policy decisions. The Reserve Bank of India has indicated a likelihood of rate hikes due to ongoing price pressures. Rural areas experienced sharper inflation increases, outpacing urban regions this month.

item.title: Centre & states to draft rules for existing arrest cases under GST
item.description: The Centre will collaborate with states to create standard procedures for handling arrest cases. Starting April 1, 2027, an invoice management system will be mandatory, minimizing human errors during digital matching. A quarterly review of GST refund risk assessment will also be implemented to maintain consistency across jurisdictions. The proposed changes aim to decriminalize several GST offences and decrease litigation for businesses.

item.title: India draws $351 billion in greenfield FDI, outpaces China
item.description: Speaking to ET, Nikolaus Lang, managing director & senior partner at BCG highlighted the Indian market as the biggest draw for investors amid a sweeping global realignment. He, however, stressed on sustained focus on infrastructure development, skilling and cost competitiveness for India to further enhance its manufacturing footprint on a global scale.

item.title: Wheat sowing faces heat from water shortage this winter
item.description: Farmers in India are likely to reduce wheat planting this winter due to water scarcity and low minimum support prices. Regions such as Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh may see the most significant impact from these conditions. The state governments are encouraging farmers to consider crops that require less water, which may lead to a shift in crop choices.

item.title: Assocham seeks review of bidders' qualificationfor transmission units
item.description: Assocham has suggested that the ministry improve technical qualification requirements for companies involved in transmission projects. This proposal aims to ensure that only experienced developers participate in the bidding process. The current framework allows companies to qualify based on broad infrastructure experience, which may delay project execution. The association recommends that qualifications be tailored to project value, voltage class, and complexity.

item.title: UK announces £1 billion in new commercial deals with India
item.description: The two sides also agreed to exchange data annually on the use of CETA, which came into effect on July 15. The data will cover businesses' claims for lower tariffs and feedback on implementation, beginning a year after the pact comes into force. "Communities across the UK and India are set to benefit from over £1 billion in new deals.

item.title: GST officers will soon be allowed to stop vehicles for inspection only at origin & destination states
item.description: New regulations will allow GST officers to halt vehicles carrying high-value goods only at their origin and destination. Prior authorization from a senior officer will be required for these inspections. The new provisions aim to prevent arbitrary vehicle stoppages in transit states, which have been a concern for businesses. E-way bills and required documents will still be necessary for verifying goods information.

item.title: GST Council reforms address key industry concerns, focus shifts to implementation, says Dept of Revenue official
item.description: During the 57th GST Council meeting, significant recommendations were made to address concerns from stakeholders. The government plans to implement these reforms collectively with state administrations to ensure uniformity. A working group will review issues related to input tax credit eligibility and supplier tax payments, aiming to relieve genuine taxpayers. The Bangalore Chamber of Industry and Commerce shared proposals to simplify GST compliance and policies.

item.title: Government allows 5,841 tonnes of sugar export to EU under quota-based duty concession scheme
item.description: "The quantity of 5,841 MT of sugar to be exported to the EU from India under TRQ (tariff rate quota) for the year 2026-27 (October 2026 to September 2027) has been notified," the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) has said in a public notice dated October 9.

item.title: Centre to set up high-level committee within a week to address sugarcane farmers' grievances
item.description: Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Food Minister Pralhad Joshi held detailed discussions at the Pusa campus with a delegation of farmers from the two major sugarcane-growing states. About 80-90 farmers from different organisations attended, along with state ministers.

item.title: From pharma to Scotch whisky, UK has "huge" export potential in India: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal
item.description: Speaking at the India-UK JETCO Business Plenary on Monday, Goyal highlighted the complementary nature of the two economies and stressed the need to strengthen economic partnerships to unlock new growth opportunities.

item.title: Indian rice exporters find a way through disruptions to retain competitiveness in Gulf market
item.description: Indian rice exporters have partnered with Eximwala Solutions to utilise bulk shipping for their products with an aim to significantly lower freight costs by about 74%, enhancing competitiveness. The shipments will mainly target the Gulf region, where demand for Basmati rice is substantial.

item.title: Noida’s new Sports City plan approved: Authority tells SC 70% of land will be reserved for sports facilities as stalled Sector 150 project moves towards revival
item.description: Noida Authority has approved the revised layout plan for the 300-acre Sports City project in Sector 150, reserving 70% of the land for sports facilities. The approval follows years of stalled development and comes as the Supreme Court examines separate cases involving Sports City projects. While four housing projects have received conditional occupancy certificates, further approvals and legal proceedings will determine the next steps for construction and homebuyers awaiting possession.

item.title: India's retail inflation quickens to 5.54% in September from 4.83% in August, hits near two-year high
item.description: India's retail inflation accelerated to 5.54% in September 2026, a notable rise from August's 4.83%. This jump is particularly linked to rising food prices, predominantly in vegetables. Rural inflation hit 6.08%, outpacing urban inflation at 4.88%. In response, the Reserve Bank of India increased the benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points on October 7, 2026, and revised its inflation outlook for the fiscal year 2027.

item.title: Trump has learnt his India lesson the hard way. Will he own up?
item.description: Donald Trump, who imposed an additional 25% tariff on Indian imports to pressure New Delhi to stop buying Russian oil, has agreed to bring Russian diesel into global markets as US fuel prices rise ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.

item.title: Piyush Goyal sees India becoming global car hub as Europe’s regulations hurt competitiveness
item.description: Piyush Goyal stated that automakers in Europe may consider manufacturing in India due to stringent regulations. He remarked that India is on the path to becoming a global car manufacturing hub. Goyal referenced challenges faced by Tata Motors after acquiring Jaguar, highlighting the need for re-engineering. The ministry has set an ambitious target of $1 trillion in exports this fiscal year.

item.title: SC urged to urgently list contempt plea over alleged release of GM rice
item.description: The Supreme Court was on Monday urged to urgently hear contempt petitions alleging that the Centre violated its 2024 judgment on genetically modified (GM) crops, following the alleged approval of herbicide-tolerant GM basmati rice for cultivation.

item.title: India’s monsoon risks may raise food industry costs: D&B
item.description: India is experiencing agricultural risks attributed to monsoon conditions, which could impact food processors and poultry producers. Procurement costs and inventory needs are likely to rise significantly due to these agricultural challenges. Rice and wheat stocks provide immediate buffers against potential food-supply issues, but maize faces direct risks from production shortfalls. Affected states include Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, which contribute significantly to overall foodgrain output.

item.title: Inflation could hit 7%, forcing RBI to hike rates by 150 bps further: Report
item.description: India's inflation is projected to reach 6-7% due to increasing price pressures and consumer expectations. The Reserve Bank of India has acknowledged risks stemming from rising input costs and resilient domestic demand. Recent trends show that household inflation expectations are significantly higher than headline inflation rates. The RBI has raised its GDP growth projection while revising inflation forecasts upwards to 6% for the upcoming quarter.

item.title: India’s Rs 34,284-crore Basmati trade gets a logistics boost with Iraq shipping plan
item.description: IREF has introduced a bulk-shipping initiative aimed at cutting freight costs for Basmati rice exports to Iraq. This initiative will lower costs from USD 350 to USD 90 per tonne, significantly improving competitiveness in the Middle East market. The collaboration with Eximwala Solutions Pte. Ltd. involves bulk shipments totaling 1,02,210 metric tonnes. The initiative is part of efforts to strengthen India’s position in global rice exports.

item.title: Waterlogging damages paddy stocks in Fazilka, Ambala as farmers blame poor drainage
item.description: Heavy rainfall has caused severe waterlogging in grain markets across Punjab and Haryana, resulting in significant damage. Farmers have reported that lakhs of quintals of stored paddy are now soaked and ruined. Lack of drainage infrastructure has been identified as a primary issue contributing to this situation. Continued rainfall is forecast, raising concerns about additional damages to crops already affected.

item.title: China's trade restrictions for services exporters under review
item.description: India is proactively gathering insights on the trade hurdles faced by its services exporters in China, engaging with industry representatives to address concerns. The investigation encompasses aspects like licensing, data regulations, and the challenges faced by Indian professionals in movement. Despite a potential of $8.95 billion in services exports to China in 2024, there's room for improvement through better partnerships and streamlined regulations, especially in mutual recognition and certification standards.

item.title: GST e-invoicing may cover services imports from unregistered companies
item.description: The Indian government is set to enhance GST reporting for imported services through e-invoicing. This expansion will affect businesses with an annual turnover exceeding ₹5 crore. Companies will need to modify their documentation processes to comply with the new regulations. Proposed changes aim to reduce mismatches between tax liabilities and input tax credits. The consultation on these changes is expected to begin shortly, with implementation likely in April 2027.

item.title: Pressure on rupee may continue after temporary gains on RBI actions, say economists
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India has implemented emergency measures to stabilize the rupee, which is facing strong global pressure. Analysts indicate that the rupee may continue to decline despite these efforts. The rupee's drop is influenced by rising US bond yields and significant foreign investment outflows. Measures such as transaction limits and cash reserve requirements are aimed at curbing speculation.

item.title: Tea Board pushes for more transparent, efficient tea auctions
item.description: Tea Board India held a seminar to discuss reforms for improving the Pan-India e-Auction system. It focused on enhancing transparency and efficiency in India’s tea auction process. The reforms have led to increased buyer participation and higher tea auction volumes over recent years. A new web-based tea auction platform is being introduced to further streamline operations and reduce costs.

item.title: RBI's rupee defence may drain banking liquidity, ease currency pressure
item.description: RBI has introduced measures to curb rupee volatility, which could ease immediate depreciation pressures in the currency market. These measures include limiting foreign exchange derivative contracts and increasing hedging costs for importers. Experts predict that these actions may lead to a reduction in USD/INR rates and forward premiums. However, external factors like crude oil prices may still pose challenges.

item.title: India's services demand outlook positive for Q3FY27, margin concerns persist: RBI
item.description: India's services sector is expected to maintain a positive demand outlook in Q3FY27, although business optimism has moderated compared with the previous quarter, with firms anticipating some easing in cost pressures but remaining less optimistic about selling prices and profit margins, according to the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) latest Services and Infrastructure Outlook Survey.

item.title: Need to look at cost of doing business to boost manufacturing; cut statutory liquidity ratio: Amitabh Kant
item.description: Amitabh Kant has advocated for reducing the statutory liquidity ratio to promote job-intensive manufacturing in India. He emphasized that cutting SLR could lower the cost of credit for businesses. Kant highlighted the importance of adequate credit in supporting the growth of startups in new-age sectors. Additionally, he addressed the need for easier land acquisition and better power availability for manufacturers.

item.title: India’s rupee defence raises question of how far RBI will go
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India implemented strong measures to stabilise the rupee as external pressures intensify. This includes opening a dollar window for state-owned oil refiners and introducing a new reserve requirement for foreign-exchange derivatives. Analysts expect the rupee to rally but caution that sustaining those gains may be difficult due to high oil prices and foreign fund outflows.

item.title: India has the hair, China has the wigs: Inside a $940 million trade
item.description: Indian hair has emerged as a sought-after commodity on the international stage, prized for its vibrant hues and high quality. Yet, the country is encountering significant challenges due to the smuggling of raw hair to China, creating a shortage. The market for processed hair, essential for wigs and extensions, remains limited in India.

item.title: India expanding trade footprint to strengthen global ties and empower MSMEs: Piyush Goyal
item.description: India is increasing its network of free trade agreements (FTAs) to integrate deeply with global economies. Nine trade pacts covering 38 developed economies have been concluded in the past four and a half years. The trade pacts are not merely confined to bureacratic corridors but also include discussions with stakeholders. India is wrapping up deals with Canada and UK while pursuing energy deals with GCC and trade relations in West Asia and Americas.

item.title: Fading Aroma of Black Cardamom: A $480 million market may bloom while India's 'black gold' wilts
item.description: India’s large black cardamom industry is battling declining plantation health, crop diseases and climate change, threatening farmers’ livelihoods in Sikkim. Once the world’s largest producer, India has lost ground to Nepal, which now dominates global production. The Sikkim government is backing scientific research, improved planting material and disease-resistant varieties to revive the state’s valuable black gold crop.

item.title: US trade deal to be finalised as 'circumstances have changed': Piyush Goyal
item.description: India is reassessing its interim trade agreement framework with the US in light of recent global shifts. Commerce minister Piyush Goyal indicated that negotiations are active with nations like Mexico, the UK, and Canada. Additionally, alternative trade discussions are being held with several countries. The export statistics up to September reflect strong performance, indicating optimistic prospects ahead.

item.title: RBI tightens rules for forex bets to shield bruised rupee
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India has tightened regulations on foreign exchange derivatives to stabilize the rupee's value. New measures include stricter documentation requirements and lowering transaction limits for forex contracts. A special window will cater to the daily dollar needs of specific oil marketing companies. These actions aim to reduce speculative dollar demand and enhance market discipline. Bankers suggest these measures could impact the rupee's market value and trading activity.

item.title: 300-member Canadian trade delegation heads to India as countries look to firm up ties
item.description: Canada is preparing to send a significant trade delegation to India, aiming to enhance commercial relationships. Led by Minister Maninder Sidhu, the mission will focus on expanding partnerships in aerospace, agri-food, and clean technology. This event will coincide with ongoing negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement aimed at elevating bilateral trade. Canadian businesses hope to connect with Indian leaders and boost employability in Canada.

item.title: RBI may raise repo rate by 75-100 bps in current cycle: Report
item.description: SBI Capital Markets expects the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to raise the repo rate by 75-100 basis points during the current tightening cycle, with a larger hike in December 2026 possible depending on inflation data. The report projects consumer inflation to peak in Q3 FY27 before easing, while warning that high crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions and rising borrowing costs could weigh on consumption. Higher rates may support bank margins in FY27, with bonds potentially regaining investor interest in FY28.

item.title: RBI steps in to support rupee as currency nears record low; tightens forex rules
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India has announced new measures aimed at stabilizing the rupee's value in foreign exchange markets. These measures include tightening foreign exchange derivative norms and creating a special window for oil marketing companies. By implementing a cash reserve requirement for large forex derivatives, the central bank seeks to curb speculative dollar demand. The impact of these interventions is expected to affect the rupee's value and forward premiums.

item.title: India needs open trade, a stronger WTO and a more proactive global role: Experts
item.description: India's economic growth necessitates a stronger alignment of domestic priorities with international trade positions and agreements. The discussion highlighted the ongoing importance of the World Trade Organisation in shaping global trade rules. Experts emphasized the need for India to actively engage in multilateral trade systems while pursuing Free Trade Agreements. They also discussed India's potential to contribute its vision of sustainability in trade.

item.title: RBI moves to support rupee at 96.78, cracks down on forex derivatives
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India introduced new measures to address the pressure on the rupee. These measures include tightening foreign exchange derivative rules and limiting rebooking of cancelled contracts. Furthermore, a 20% cash reserve requirement has been established for large forex derivatives transactions. The central bank aims to enhance market discipline and promote effective risk management strategies.

item.title: Food industry warns of supply shock over Super El Nino
item.description: India's food industry is alerting to a potential supply shock projected for the year 2027. Experts indicate that a Super El Nino may disrupt crop production and elevate food inflation. Growing concerns arise over the impact on sugar and oilseed production, particularly in states with severe drought conditions. The livestock sector is also preparing for increased feed costs due to these challenges.

item.title: GST Council proposes 2% TDS on scrap deals
item.description: The proposed levy covers plastic waste, discarded tyres, electrical and electronic scrap, and used cooking oil. Under the framework, registered buyers will have to deduct TDS when purchasing from registered suppliers and pay GST under RCM on purchases from unregistered sellers, even when the latter fall below the GST registration threshold.

item.title: Statistics ministry proposes common framework to calculate state GDP
item.description: The statistics ministry has proposed a common framework for estimating state gross domestic product. This framework uses an expenditure approach under the revised 2022-23 base year. Currently, no state compiles estimates of private final consumption expenditure, creating a gap. Proposed methods include using administrative data to allocate estimates across states and union territories. This initiative aims to improve consistency and comparability of GSDP estimates throughout India.

item.title: Rural job demand under VB-G RAM G jumps 25% in September, 15.6 million households seek work
item.description: In September, the demand for work under the VB-G RAM G scheme increased by 25.2% compared to August. Approximately 15.6 million households sought work under the program, significantly rising from 12.5 million in August. The number of people seeking employment also grew to 18.8 million from 15.4 million in August. This scheme was launched in July, providing guaranteed annual employment of 125 days.

item.title: Highway projects get three more months of bitumen, diesel cost escalation cover amid West Asia crisis
item.description: The ministry of road transport and highways is extending the cost compensation for bitumen and diesel. This extension will apply to projects executed until December 31, 2026. Work carried out will only qualify if the bid due date was set before April 1, 2026. The compensation aims to address the impact of rising diesel prices on highway construction.

item.title: Global trade to grow 4% in 2026, slower than 4.4% in 2025: UNCTAD
item.description: Global trade is projected to grow by 4% in 2026, although slower than the previous year. The report indicates higher trade values resulting from energy price increases and export controls. Trade between China and the US has decreased significantly, while East Asia is expanding trade with both regions. Developing economies, particularly India, are expected to drive notable growth despite overall global economic slowdowns.

item.title: FM Nirmala Sitharaman meets Singapore President, PM; discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation
item.description: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman visited Singapore from October 9 to 11 for official discussions. She met President Tharman Shanmugaratnam and Prime Minister Lawrence Wong to strengthen bilateral relations. Their discussions focused on economic developments and investment opportunities for Singaporean companies in India. Sitharaman also met Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, who highlighted the growth prospects in India. Singapore is India's largest source of foreign direct investment, significantly contributing to the economy.

item.title: India's forex reserves fall $12.95 billion to $734.60 billion in week ended October 2
item.description: India's foreign exchange reserves have dropped by $12.95 billion to $734.60 billion as of October 2. This decline was influenced by a reduction in foreign currency assets and gold reserves. The previous week, reserves had already decreased by $18.34 billion, falling to $747.56 billion. The Reserve Bank of India reported these figures in its recent data release. Fluctuations in reserves are a significant aspect of India's economic landscape.

item.title: Next round of review meeting of ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement to be held in Jan
item.description: India and ASEAN will hold the next review meeting of their goods trade agreement in January 2027, as both sides push to speed up negotiations on updating the 2009 pact. The joint committee has asked sub-groups to clear pending chapters and work to firm timelines, with ASEAN accounting for about 11% of India’s global trade.

item.title: GST Council bets on faster refunds, lower penalties to ease business burden
item.description: The 57th GST Council meeting has introduced measures to simplify compliance and expedite refunds for businesses. Recommendations include increasing the prosecution threshold and reducing penalties for non-compliance. The proposed framework features faster acknowledgement timelines for claims and provisional refunds for taxpayers. Changes to the inverted-duty structure are set to unlock credits in various sectors including textiles and manufacturing.

item.title: Centre seeks fishers’ views to shape national action plan for sustainable small-scale fisheries
item.description: The Union Department of Fisheries is leading the consultation process, with the Bay of Bengal Programme Inter-Governmental Organisation (BOBP-IGO) facilitating and coordinating the exercise.
